svg.title: The Woman at the Well
svg.desc: A one-minute comic in 5 panels. Panel 1 (John 4:5-7): Jesus sits tired beside the stone rim of Jacob's well; a Samaritan woman walks up carrying a water jar. Caption: "Jacob's well at Sychar, about noon. John calls it a spring, πηγή." Jesus says: "Give me a drink." Note: "Watch who says which word. John 4 splits them by speaker; elsewhere the two can overlap." Panel 2 (John 4:11): The woman, jar in hand, speaks to Jesus; above her head a thought cloud shows a deep shaft cut through rock to water far below, with a rope and a jar let down. The woman pictures a deep shaft, labelled "φρέαρ: a shaft". The woman says: "Sir, you have nothing to draw water with, and the well is deep." Panel 3 (John 4:13-14): Jesus, seated, answers; above His head a thought cloud shows water rising out of the rock on its own and running over. Jesus pictures a spring rising out of the rock, labelled "πηγή: a spring". Jesus says: "The water that I will give him will become in him a spring of water welling up to eternal life." Panel 4 (John 4:15): The woman asks for the water; the thought cloud over her head still shows the shaft. The woman pictures the deep shaft again, labelled "φρέαρ". The woman says: "Sir, give me this water, so that I will not be thirsty or have to come here to draw water." Note: "The study's reading: she still pictures the shaft." Panel 5 (John 4:26-29): Jesus sits by the well; the woman's water jar stands on the ground where she left it, and she hurries away toward the town with a question mark over her head. Caption: "She leaves her water jar and goes into the town." Jesus says: "I who speak to you am he." The woman says: "Can this be the Christ?" The point: She came to a shaft; Jesus offered a spring, the Holy Spirit welling up inside whoever asks. Ask Him, and drink (John 4:10, 14; 7:39).
svg.text: A shaft, a spring, and the One who gives it, in one minute
